parts.latex: Calculate the mean and the range of goals that Sophie scored throughout the season.
Use calculations to determine whether any of Sophie's scores are outliers.

criteria: Correct answer
Correct mean or correct range, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The quartiles of the data are
$$Q_1 = 5, \quad Q_3 = 11$$
so the interquartile range is
$$IQR = 11 - 5 = 6$$
Outliers lie below $Q_1 - 1.5\times IQR$ or above $Q_3 + 1.5\times IQR$.
$$\begin{aligned} Q_1 - 1.5\times IQR &= 5 - 1.5\times 6 = -4 \\ Q_3 + 1.5\times IQR &= 11 + 1.5\times 6 = 20 \end{aligned}$$
Since $24 > 20$, 24 is an outlier.
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the outlier boundaries $-4$ and $20$, or equivalent merit
Finds $Q_1$, $Q_3$ and $IQR$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The five-number summary of a dataset is given.

Lowest score $= 1$

Lower quartile $(Q_1) = 4$

Median $(Q_2) = 7$

Upper quartile $(Q_3) = 10$

Highest score $= 20$

Is 20 an outlier? Justify your answer with calculations.

solutions.latex:
The interquartile range is
$$\begin{aligned} IQR &= Q_3 - Q_1 \\ &= 10 - 4 \\ &= 6 \end{aligned}$$
An outlier lies above $Q_3 + 1.5\times IQR$.
$$\begin{aligned} Q_3 + 1.5\times IQR &= 10 + 1.5\times 6 \\ &= 19 \end{aligned}$$
Since $20 > 19$, 20 is an outlier.
criteria: Correct answer
Attempts to use $Q_3+1.5\times IQR$, or calculates the interquartile range

parts.latex:
The heights, in centimetres, of 10 players on a basketball team are shown.

$$170, 180, 185, 188, 192, 193, 193, 194, 196, 202$$

Is the height of the shortest player on the team considered an outlier? Justify your answer with calculations.

solutions.latex:
The lower and upper quartiles are $Q_1=185$ and $Q_3=194$.
$$\begin{aligned} IQR &= 194-185 \\ &= 9 \end{aligned}$$
A value is an outlier if it is less than
$$\begin{aligned} Q_1-1.5\times IQR &= 185-1.5\times 9 \\ &= 171.5 \end{aligned}$$
Since $170<171.5$, the shortest height is considered an outlier.
criteria: Correct answer
Calculates the interquartile range, or equivalent merit
Finds a quartile, or equivalent merit

6042.stem:
The number of cars parked in a carpark is recorded each day for thirteen days. The dataset is listed in ascending order:

$$12, 15, 15, 17, 19, 20, 22, 24, 25, 27, 28, 30 \text{ and } m.$$

parts.latex: What is the interquartile range of this dataset?
What is the greatest value of $m$ such that this dataset has no outlier?

solutions.latex:
With 13 scores, the lower half is the first 6 scores and the upper half is the last 6 scores.

The lower quartile is the average of the 3rd and 4th scores:
$$Q_1 = \dfrac{15+17}{2} = 16$$
The upper quartile is the average of the 10th and 11th scores:
$$Q_3 = \dfrac{27+28}{2} = 27.5$$
$$\begin{aligned} IQR &= Q_3 - Q_1 \\ &= 27.5 - 16 \\ &= 11.5 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the lower or upper quartile, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
An outlier lies above $Q_3 + 1.5 \times IQR$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Upper bound} &= 27.5 + 1.5 \times 11.5 \\ &= 44.75 \end{aligned}$$
Since the number of cars is a whole number, the greatest value of $m$ with no outlier is $44$.
$$\therefore\ m = 44$$
criteria: Correct answer
Attempts to find the upper bound, or equivalent merit

6115.stem:
Mike completes ten spelling tests and receives the following scores:

$$10, 11, 11, 12, 14, 14, 16, 19, 19, 20$$

parts.latex: What is Mike's standard deviation? Give your answer correct to one decimal place
If Mike scores 5 in the next spelling test, will it be considered an outlier? Justify your answer with mathematical calculations.

criteria: Correct answer

solutions.latex:
From the ordered data:
$$Q_1 = 11, \quad Q_3 = 19, \quad \text{IQR} = 8$$
Lower outlier boundary:
$$\begin{aligned} Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR} &= 11 - 1.5 \times 8 \\ &= -1 \end{aligned}$$
Since $5 > -1$, a score of $5$ is not below the boundary.
$$\therefore\ \text{not an outlier}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the quartiles and IQR, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The number of thorns on a variety of rose bushes were recorded in a stem-and-leaf plot.

The leaf from the first entry is shown as “$x$”.

\extable{717_q26_t1}

What is the largest value of $x$ for which this entry could be considered an outlier?

solutions.latex:
From the stem-and-leaf plot:
$$\begin{aligned}Q_1&=36\\Q_2&=42\\Q_3&=51\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}IQR&=51-36\\&=15\end{aligned}$$
An outlier lies below the lower fence $Q_1-1.5\times IQR$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Lower fence}&=36-(1.5\times 15)\\&=13.5\end{aligned}$$
So an outlier is less than 13.5.
$$\therefore\ x=3$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the lower fence, or equivalent merit
Finds the interquartile range, or equivalent merit
Finds the quartiles, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The heights of students in a class are represented in the boxplot below.

\exfigure{850_q6_1}

A new student, who will become the tallest member, is joining the class.

What is the maximum height the new student can be in order to not be classified as an outlier?

solutions.latex:
A student is an outlier if their height is above $Q_3+1.5\times IQR$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Upper bound}&=Q_3+1.5\times IQR\\&=170+1.5\times(170-155)\\&=192.5\end{aligned}$$
Any student taller than 192.5 cm is an outlier.

Hence the maximum height is 192.5 cm, option B.
criteria: Correct answer
